title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.14228v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Pixel-space world models have recently emerged as a promising approach for GUI agents, predicting future screens prior to execution and subsequently re-perceiving them for action selection. However, this two-stage paradigm faces two key challenges in GUI environments: (L1) the high computational cost of pixel reconstruction and (L2) the need to reconstruct large and diverse appearance-level details beyond what is required for action selection. In practice, this screen-generation objective can induce an identity shortcut problem, where future-state prediction largely preserves the current state rather than capturing action-induced changes. In this work, we reformulate GUI world modeling by shifting the prediction target from full-screen reconstruction to action-induced future information in latent space. translated_title: 面向GUI智能体的潜在世界动作模型
translated_abstract: 像素空间世界模型近来已成为GUI智能体的一种有前景的方法，它在执行动作之前预测未来的屏幕，随后重新感知这些屏幕以进行动作选择。然而，这种两阶段范式在GUI环境中面临两个关键挑战：(L1) 像素重建的高计算成本；(L2) 需要重建大量超出动作选择所需的外观级细节。在实践中，这种屏幕生成目标会引发“恒等捷径”问题，即未来状态的预测在很大程度上保留了当前状态，而未能捕捉由动作引起的变化。在本工作中，我们通过将预测目标从全屏重建转变为潜在空间中由动作引起的未来信息，重新构建了GUI世界建模。具体而言，我们利用大型多模态模型作为潜在世界模型，其共享表示支持两个专用头（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出潜在世界动作模型（Latent World Action Model），将GUI智能体的世界建模从像素级全屏重建转变为在潜在空间中预测动作引起的未来信息，从而避免了像素重建的高计算成本和恒等捷径问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Latent World Action Model that shifts GUI world modeling from pixel-space full-screen reconstruction to predicting action-induced future information in latent space, leveraging a large multimodal model to avoid high computational costs and the identity shortcut problem.
